record_note: Wired by hand on 2026-09-18 (commit 3ee8251, 'ci: local gate runner + git hooks (no GitHub); format drift fixed; tidy clean'), before the kit existed as a git repo — so `revision` is the kit's FIRST PUBLISHED commit, not the exact copy point; do not read it as the tree this repo was copied from. The direction here is the reverse of the other recorded repos': JSOM's gate is one of the three real instances the kit's templates were generalised FROM (DESIGN-NOTES.md section 1 — the 2026-09-19 MoA design pass carried 'JSOM's tools/ci.sh + both hooks + .ci.env.example' verbatim in its prompt), and the only kit-to-repo traffic since is the tidy-baseline fix ported in 67302cc (card t_1eab5d69, already applied to all four files below). Two artifacts in the convention's C++ set have no entry because this repo never took them: INCIDENTS.md was never copied (grep -rn INCIDENTS over the repo returns nothing) and there is no kit-derived agent contract — CLAUDE.md is this repo's own, predating the kit (2026-02-15, extended 2026-09-08 and 2026-09-19) and following a different design from templates/CLAUDE.md.template, so a sync must never overwrite it. Synced on 2026-09-20 by card t_d899b8ff (the commit that carries this hash update): the four gate-contract rules this script used to predate — a final GATE PASSED/GATE FAILED token (it used to print only 'all N stage(s) passed in Xs'), BLOCK lines for every requested stage that did not run, export NO_COLOR=1 (this script greps tool output, and ANSI escapes defeat the greps), and a derived rather than hard-coded usage header range (was sed -n '2,21p') — plus the end-of-run summary the kit and jsonTools both print. Both hooks gained the kit's provenance line, with their deviation stated there instead of pointing at an INCIDENTS.md this repo does not have. Rule that keeps this file true: any commit that edits a copied artifact must update that artifact's repo_sha256 in the same commit. **2026-09-20, card t_0cc793fb:** the `kitprobes` stage and `tools/kit-probes/tidy-baseline.sh` were taken from the kit at the revision above — a fix that must propagate ships a probe, and this copy now runs it in its own gate. `revision` moved to that commit because these entries come from it; the earlier entries are still the fb387f2 wiring, and the kit files behind them have not changed between the two commits (the ones that did — `templates/cpp/ci.sh`, `templates/hooks/pre-push` — were ported in this same commit). **2026-09-20 (still card t_0cc793fb):** two more artifacts from the same kit revision are recorded here — the gate's dispatch guards (a stage that dies or returns non-zero without a verdict can no longer leave a green run; measured on this gate's own `local -a sources`) and that fix's own probe `tools/kit-probes/gate-stage-guards.sh`. **2026-09-20, card t_772eabd9:** JSOM's CMakeLists no longer writes CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE or CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX into the cache as a subdirectory (both did so with FORCE until this commit, which is how it configured its CONSUMERS: Computo's Pages workflow passes no build type, inherited Release, and compiled at -O3 for months until a gcc 13/14 false positive in libstdc++'s <variant> took its only production target offline — cards t_93e9a66b and t_772eabd9, OPTIMIZATIONS.md #2), and CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS is top-level only for the same reason. That guard has a gate stage: `consumer` runs tools/consumer_probe.sh on every run, which is why tools/ci.sh, .ci.env.example and .githooks/pre-push (its stage list) are re-hashed in this commit. `revision` is unchanged: no kit file moved, so nothing here comes from a new kit commit. **2026-09-20, card t_fb62d8fa:** the record gained the kit's per-fix lists (docs/KIT-REVISION-CONVENTION.md, 'Exact file shape'), so what this copy has and has not taken from the kit is machine-readable instead of prose. `adopted_fixes` names the two probes this copy carries, with the kit revision each fix came from -- and that claim is now CHECKED, not just asserted: the record checker runs each probe against tools/ci.sh, and a claim whose probe is absent or fails is a record failure. `declined_fixes` records the kit's `optimized-build-stage` (probe `probes/optimized-stage.sh`, added by the kit at d531a110) as NOT TAKEN: run against this gate it FAILS (measured 0 ok, 7 failed at this HEAD), and whether this fork takes that stage is parked with Harri. Saying so in the record is the point -- the alternative, moving `revision` to d531a110, would claim this copy was wired from artifacts it never took. **`revision` and every `kit_sha256` are UNCHANGED by this commit**: nothing here came from the kit, and being behind the kit is not a failure -- the check that called it one was measuring whether the kit had moved. **2026-09-20, card t_0a9a0018:** the kit's GIT_INDEX_FILE fix was ported — kit f9c3300 — as one line in tools/ci.sh's prologue plus the kit's own probe at tools/kit-probes/git-index-file.sh, and `revision` moved to f9c3300 because this files[] set now takes that probe from it. Nothing else this copy carries changed between the two revisions, so every other entry's `kit_sha256` is untouched; the one that did move is tools/ci.sh's, because the kit's templates/cpp/ci.sh is where the fix landed. JSOM is the exposed case in its own right: CMakeLists.txt FetchContents googletest, benchmark and nlohmann_json, so a cold `build` (or `pristine`) has cmake running `git status` inside build/_deps/<dep>-src — the same shape that failed a pathspec commit on Computo (cards t_9541aa62 -> t_0a9a0018). `adopted_fixes` claims the fix and the record checker RUNS the probe against this repo's gate. **2026-10-06, record re-hash:** the checker reported this record BAD on repo_sha256 mismatch for 3 entries, edited after the record was written without this file being updated in the same commit — the one rule the convention says keeps it true. Re-hashed, no other field changed: tools/ci.sh (last edited f10faae 2026-09-21 fuzz: consume JSONFuzz as a library at its release tag, not as hand-listed sources); .ci.env.example (last edited f10faae 2026-09-21 fuzz: consume JSONFuzz as a library at its release tag, not as hand-listed sources); .githooks/pre-push (last edited e9497e6 2026-09-20 docs: stop the documentation from lying, and gate it). **2026-10-06, hook-tier port:** adopted_fixes gains hook-tiers-agree (from_revision 919006e, the kit commit whose probe this copy carries verbatim); tools/ci.sh gained CI_FAST_STAGES/CI_FULL_STAGES and the `fast`/`full` arguments, .githooks/pre-commit now names the tier, and both files are re-hashed here. The full tier was already the default list — this port did not change which stages run, only where the lists are written down. **2026-10-06, card t_075c0a6f (KitCI fleet batch 2 of 3):** the gate is no longer a bash script. tools/ci.sh and the probes under tools/kit-probes/ are DELETED; the gate is the tracked gate.toml (14 stages, tiers fast/full) run by kit-ci, plus scripts/gate-env.sh, scripts/gate.sh and one scripts/<stage>.sh per stage — all of them this repo's own files, which is why none appears in files[] below. files[] loses tools/ci.sh and every tools/kit-probes/*.sh entry: the artifacts are gone, so no hash can describe them. The kit fixes those probes guarded move from adopted_fixes to declined_fixes — not because the fixes were declined, but because the artifact they CHECK no longer exists (each probe is written against a single bash gate file; measured against scripts/gate.sh, see INCIDENTS.md for the verdicts). The contracts did not go: each one has a named home, listed in INCIDENTS.md entry by entry. .githooks/pre-commit and .githooks/pre-push are RE-HASHED because this commit edits them: they now NAME a tier (--tier fast, and --tier full with CI_REQUIRE_CLEAN=1, the old --require-clean flag moved into the environment), and their branch for this repo's own tools/ci.sh is gone with that file. `revision` and every other entry are UNCHANGED: nothing here came from the kit, and being behind the kit is not a failure.
